"""educational_catalog — complete catalog of all educational content.

This module defines every educational topic in Deep Space Trader as a
structured record, then exposes functions to generate reports, export
markdown, and count topics by subject. The single source of truth for
"what educational content exists" — used by Steam page generation,
the curriculum mapper, and the demo verification script.

Usage:
    python -m core.educational_catalog          # print markdown catalog
    python -m core.educational_catalog --json    # print JSON catalog
"""

import json

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Topic record structure
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Each topic maps to:
#   item_asset_name  -> the .uasset file in Content/Items/ (e.g. Basalt_Data)
#   text_level_name  -> the TextRender actor label in the .umap (e.g. EduText_Basalt)
#   source           -> abbreviated citation; full text in EDUCATIONAL_SOURCES.md

TOPICS = [
    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    # GEOLOGY  (20 topics)
    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    dict(
        id="basalt",
        subject="geology",
        title="Basalt",
        description=(
            "Dark volcanic rock formed when magma cools rapidly at Titan's "
            "surface. Contains olivine and pyroxene crystals. Common in "
            "Titan's cryovolcanic plains, where water-ammonia magma erupts "
            "instead of molten silicate rock."
        ),
        item_asset_name="Basalt_Data",
        text_level_name="EduText_Basalt",
        source="USGS Basalt fact sheet; Marshak (2019) Earth: Portrait of a Planet Ch.6",
    ),
    dict(
        id="granite",
        subject="geology",
        title="Granite",
        description=(
            "Coarse-grained igneous rock that forms deep underground "
            "from slow-cooling magma. Its crystals (feldspar, quartz, mica) "
            "grow large given enough time — a lesson in patience written in "
            "stone."
        ),
        item_asset_name="Granite_Data",
        text_level_name="EduText_Granite",
        source="USGS Granite fact sheet; Blatt, Tracy & Owens (2006) Petrology Ch.4",
    ),
    dict(
        id="obsidian",
        subject="geology",
        title="Obsidian",
        description=(
            "Volcanic glass formed when lava cools so fast that crystals "
            "cannot form. Used by ancient civilizations for cutting tools. "
            "On Titan, similar rapid cooling occurs at cryovolcanic vents "
            "where water-ammonia magma hits the frigid surface."
        ),
        item_asset_name="Obsidian_Data",
        text_level_name="EduText_Obsidian",
        source="USGS Obsidian fact sheet; HyperPhysics (Georgia State)",
    ),
    dict(
        id="pumice",
        subject="geology",
        title="Pumice",
        description=(
            "Volcanic froth lighter than water. Pumice forms when gas-rich "
            "lava cools so fast it traps bubbles. Floating pumice rafts can "
            "travel across oceans, carrying life between worlds — a key "
            "mechanism in the panspermia hypothesis."
        ),
        item_asset_name="Pumice_Data",
        text_level_name="EduText_Pumice",
        source="USGS Pumice; Marshak (2019) §6.3; Bryan et al. (2012) Geology",
    ),
    dict(
        id="sandstone",
        subject="geology",
        title="Sandstone",
        description=(
            "Sedimentary rock made of sand grains cemented together. Each "
            "grain tells a story of wind and water that shaped ancient "
            "landscapes. On Titan, methane-driven dunes create similar "
            "layered deposits stretching hundreds of kilometres."
        ),
        item_asset_name="Sandstone_Data",
        text_level_name="EduText_Sandstone",
        source="USGS Sandstone; Lorenz (2014) Titan Unveiled",
    ),
    dict(
        id="limestone",
        subject="geology",
        title="Limestone",
        description=(
            "Marine sedimentary rock formed from the shells of ancient sea "
            "creatures. Its presence on any world indicates a past ocean — a "
            "key clue in exoplanet habitability studies and Earth's deep "
            "geological history."
        ),
        item_asset_name="Limestone_Data",
        text_level_name="EduText_Limestone",
        source="USGS Limestone; Blatt et al. (2006) §7.2",
    ),
    dict(
        id="shale",
        subject="geology",
        title="Shale",
        description=(
            "Fine-grained sedimentary rock formed from compacted mud and "
            "clay. Shale preserves ancient organic matter and fossils better "
            "than any other rock type. On Titan, similar deposits could "
            "contain clues to prebiotic chemistry."
        ),
        item_asset_name="Shale_Data",
        text_level_name="EduText_Shale",
        source="USGS Shale; Blatt et al. (2006) §7.1",
    ),
    dict(
        id="marble",
        subject="geology",
        title="Marble",
        description=(
            "Metamorphosed limestone. Heat and pressure recrystallise "
            "limestone into marble — nature's kiln transforming one rock "
            "into another without melting. The same process on Titan would "
            "require deep burial or cryovolcanic heat."
        ),
        item_asset_name="Marble_Data",
        text_level_name="EduText_Marble",
        source="USGS Marble; Blatt et al. (2006) Ch.9",
    ),
    dict(
        id="quartzite",
        subject="geology",
        title="Quartzite",
        description=(
            "Metamorphosed sandstone. Sandstone recrystallises into "
            "quartzite under heat and pressure, fusing sand grains into "
            "solid quartz. A lesson in transformation under stress — "
            "the rock equivalent of forging steel."
        ),
        item_asset_name="Quartzite_Data",
        text_level_name="EduText_Quartzite",
        source="USGS Quartzite; Blatt et al. (2006) §9.3",
    ),
    dict(
        id="slate",
        subject="geology",
        title="Slate",
        description=(
            "Metamorphosed shale. Low-grade metamorphism transforms shale "
            "into slate, which splits into thin, durable sheets. Used "
            "historically for roofing — nature's testimony to the power "
            "of gentle, sustained pressure over millions of years."
        ),
        item_asset_name="Slate_Data",
        text_level_name="EduText_Slate",
        source="USGS Slate; Blatt et al. (2006) §9.1",
    ),
    dict(
        id="igneous",
        subject="geology",
        title="Igneous Collection",
        description=(
            "Igneous rocks form from cooling magma or lava. Their crystal "
            "size tells you the cooling history: large crystals mean slow "
            "cooling deep underground; small or absent crystals mean rapid "
            "cooling at the surface. The entire rock cycle begins here."
        ),
        item_asset_name="Igneous_Data",
        text_level_name="EduText_Igneous",
        source="Marshak (2019) Ch.6; USGS Igneous Rocks",
    ),
    dict(
        id="sedimentary",
        subject="geology",
        title="Sedimentary Collection",
        description=(
            "Sedimentary rocks form from layers of sand, mud, or organic "
            "matter compressed over millions of years. They preserve "
            "fossils, ripples, and ancient environments — the library of "
            "Earth's geological history, page by page."
        ),
        item_asset_name="Sedimentary_Data",
        text_level_name="EduText_Sedimentary",
        source="Blatt et al. (2006) Ch.7; USGS Sedimentary Rocks",
    ),
    dict(
        id="metamorphic",
        subject="geology",
        title="Metamorphic Collection",
        description=(
            "Metamorphic rocks form when existing rocks are transformed by "
            "heat and pressure in the solid state — no melting required. "
            "Earth's internal engine drives this process at plate boundaries, "
            "creating new rocks from old without returning them to magma."
        ),
        item_asset_name="Metamorphic_Data",
        text_level_name="EduText_Metamorphic",
        source="Blatt et al. (2006) Ch.9; USGS Metamorphic Rocks",
    ),
    dict(
        id="cryovolcano",
        subject="geology",
        title="Titan Cryovolcanism",
        description=(
            "Titan has cryovolcanoes that erupt water and ammonia instead "
            "of molten rock. These ice volcanoes reshape the surface and "
            "release methane into the atmosphere — a geologic cycle powered "
            "by tidal heating from Saturn's gravity."
        ),
        item_asset_name="Cryovolcano_Data",
        text_level_name="EduText_Cryovolcano",
        source="Lopes et al. (2013) Icarus; NASA Cassini VIMS data",
    ),
    # Additional geology topics — created from Titan-expansion items
    dict(
        id="gneiss",
        subject="geology",
        title="Gneiss",
        description=(
            "High-grade metamorphic rock with distinct banding. Gneiss forms "
            "under extreme heat and pressure deep in the crust, where "
            "minerals segregate into light and dark layers. The bands record "
            "the direction of tectonic forces that shaped continents."
        ),
        item_asset_name="Gneiss_Data",
        text_level_name="EduText_Gneiss",
        source="Blatt et al. (2006) §9.4; USGS Metamorphic Rocks",
    ),
    dict(
        id="schist",
        subject="geology",
        title="Schist",
        description=(
            "Medium-grade metamorphic rock with visible mica crystals. "
            "Schist forms at higher temperatures than slate, allowing mica "
            "to grow large enough to see. The glittering surface is a "
            "marker of the metamorphic grade — a thermometer written in "
            "minerals."
        ),
        item_asset_name="Schist_Data",
        text_level_name="EduText_Schist",
        source="Blatt et al. (2006) §9.2; USGS Metamorphic Rocks",
    ),
    dict(
        id="andesite",
        subject="geology",
        title="Andesite",
        description=(
            "Intermediate igneous rock common at subduction zones. Named "
            "after the Andes mountains, andesite forms where oceanic crust "
            "melts as it sinks into the mantle. Its composition is halfway "
            "between basalt and granite — a geological middle ground."
        ),
        item_asset_name="Andesite_Data",
        text_level_name="EduText_Andesite",
        source="Marshak (2019) §6.5; USGS Igneous Rocks",
    ),
    dict(
        id="rhyolite",
        subject="geology",
        title="Rhyolite",
        description=(
            "Fine-grained volcanic rock with the same composition as "
            "granite. Rhyolite forms when silica-rich magma erupts at the "
            "surface and cools quickly. Its light colour comes from "
            "abundant quartz and feldspar — the same minerals in "
            "continental crust."
        ),
        item_asset_name="Rhyolite_Data",
        text_level_name="EduText_Rhyolite",
        source="Marshak (2019) §6.4; USGS Igneous Rocks",
    ),
    dict(
        id="diorite",
        subject="geology",
        title="Diorite",
        description=(
            "Coarse-grained intrusive igneous rock, intermediate in "
            "composition between granite and gabbro. Diorite's speckled "
            "appearance — white feldspar mixed with dark hornblende — "
            "reflects its dual mantle-crust origin."
        ),
        item_asset_name="Diorite_Data",
        text_level_name="EduText_Diorite",
        source="Marshak (2019) §6.5; USGS Igneous Rocks",
    ),
    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    # METEOROLOGY  (13 topics)
    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    dict(
        id="cirrus",
        subject="meteorology",
        title="Cirrus Clouds",
        description=(
            "High-altitude ice crystals. Cirrus clouds form above 6 km, "
            "where temperatures are below -30°C. Made of tiny ice crystals, "
            "they signal approaching weather changes — a high-level warning "
            "system written in the sky."
        ),
        item_asset_name="Cirrus_Data",
        text_level_name="EduText_Cirrus",
        source="NOAA Cloud Classification; WMO International Cloud Atlas",
    ),
    dict(
        id="cumulus",
        subject="meteorology",
        title="Cumulus Clouds",

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Public API
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def get_all_topics():
    """Return the full list of educational topic dictionaries."""
    return TOPICS


def get_topic(topic_id: str):
    """Return a single topic by its ``id`` field, or None if not found."""
    for t in TOPICS:
        if t["id"] == topic_id:
            return t
    return None


def get_topics_by_subject(subject: str):
    """Return all topics belonging to *subject* (geology, meteorology, astronomy)."""
    return [t for t in TOPICS if t["subject"] == subject]


def count_by_subject():
    """Return a dict mapping each subject to its topic count."""
    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
    for t in TOPICS:
        s = t["subject"]
        counts[s] = counts.get(s, 0) + 1
    return counts


def generate_catalog():
    """Print a complete formatted markdown catalog of all educational topics."""
    subjects = ["geology", "meteorology", "astronomy"]
    subject_labels = {
        "geology": "Geology — reading the rocks",
        "meteorology": "Meteorology — reading the sky",
        "astronomy": "Astronomy — reading the stars",
    }

    lines = []
    lines.append("# Deep Space Trader — Educational Content Catalog")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(
        f"**{len(TOPICS)} educational topics** across "
        f"{len(subjects)} scientific disciplines. "
        "Every fact traces to a verifiable real-world source."
    )
    lines.append("")

    grand_total = 0
    for subj in subjects:
        topics = get_topics_by_subject(subj)
        if not topics:
            continue
        lines.append(f"## {subject_labels.get(subj, subj.title())}")
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(f"**{len(topics)} topics**")
        lines.append("")
        grand_total += len(topics)

        for t in topics:
            lines.append(f"### {t['title']} (`{t['id']}`)")
            lines.append("")
            lines.append(t["description"])
            lines.append("")
            lines.append(f"- **Item asset:** `{t['item_asset_name']}`")
            lines.append(f"- **Level text:** `{t['text_level_name']}`")
            lines.append(f"- **Source:** {t['source']}")
            lines.append("")

    lines.append("---")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(f"*Total: **{grand_total}** topics. "
                 f"Generated by Chimera core/educational_catalog.py*")

    print("\n".join(lines))


def generate_json():
    """Return the full catalog as a JSON string."""
    return json.dumps(
        {
            "meta": {
                "total_topics": len(TOPICS),
                "subjects": count_by_subject(),
            },
            "topics": TOPICS,
        },
        indent=2,
        ensure_ascii=False,
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CLI entry point
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys

    if "--json" in sys.argv:
        print(generate_json())
    else:
        generate_catalog()
